summary: Valentine Ball was an Indologist and scientist who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1860–1889). He served at the Geological Survey of India (1864–1881), Trinity College Dublin (1881–1883), and was Director of the National Museum of Ireland (1883–1895).
Valentino Papesso was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bologna from circa 1907 to 1911. He later served as Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Bologna from circa 1924 to 1944.
Valeria Gazizova is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She completed her Master's thesis at the University of Oslo, studying under Hanna Havnevik and MA supervisor Per Kværne.

Valerie Hansen is a historian and sinologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania and Harvard, also learning under Victor H. Mair. She held a post at East China Normal University (2005) and has taught at Yale since circa 1993.

Valerie Stoker works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, and holds a post at Wright State University. She studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi.

Valery Evgenyevich Krasnodembsky was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (~1926–1930). He worked there as a naučnyj sotrudnik (1932–1942), at the Institute of Ethnography (1933–1937), and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1934–1942).
Vamana was an Indologist who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.

Van Austin Harvey was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale. He taught at Princeton, Southern Methodist University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Stanford University (~1978–1996).
Vandita Srivastava is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, earning a Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) between 2004 and 2007 and a Ph.D. between 2010 and 2016.

Vans Kennedy was an Indologist and linguist who served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835). He was an active member of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from 1817 and served as its President from 1831 to 1835.

Vasant Shinde is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 2006 and 2026.

Vasile Burlă was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the universities of Vienna (~1860–1863) and Graz (~1863–1865). He served as a university lecturer in Classics at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University from circa 1872 to 1901.

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogorodickij was a linguist who studied under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay at Kazan State University (~1876–1880). He became a professor there in 1888 and 1893, later serving as professor at Kazan State Pedagogical University (1922–1925).

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogoslovskij was a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and history who studied at Moscow State University (~1949–1954). He served at the University of Chicago (1957–1967) and the Institute of China and Contemporary Asia (1968).

Vasilij Ivanovič Smirnov was an Indologist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies and Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov (~1928–1932). He served as a Docent at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (1936–1937).

Vasilij Matveevič Beskrovnyj was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (1926–1930). He held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, Leningrad Oriental Institute, Saint Petersburg State University, and Moscow State University.

Vasilij Vasil'evič Brodov was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Philosophy, Literature and History. He taught at several institutions including Moscow Conservatory, Surikov Art Institute, Moscow State University, and chaired Philosophy at All-Union Correspondence Civil Engineering Institute.

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev was a sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (~1898–1902) and under Édouard Chavannes (~1906–1909). He held long-term posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1921–1951).

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Kazan State University under von Erdmann, Kowalewski, and Daniil. He served as professor at Kazan State University and Saint Petersburg State University (1855–1893).
